points.description: Gives the correct final answer 510510 (= 2·3·5·7·11·13·17), with every step of the supporting argument mathematically valid. Any wrong step or wrong final answer earns nothing. Equivalent wording and correct alternative methods are accepted.

rubric.notes: Full mark only for 510510 with a fully valid argument (every prime ≤17 divides all P(n), and none appears to a higher power, e.g. via P(p) or P(1)=17!). Any wrong step or wrong answer earns 0.
rubric.answer_key: P(1)=17!, so the gcd divides 17! and only the primes 2,3,5,7,11,13,17 can occur. For a prime p ≤ 17, if p does not divide n, the numbers kn+1 for k=0,...,p-1 cover all residues mod p, so one is divisible by p (k=0 gives 1, so the residues of kn+1 over k=0..p-1 include 0 mod p). Thus p divides P(n) for all n not divisible by p. If p divides n, then p divides the factor n itself. So every such prime divides every P(n). For the exponent: take n=p (p ≤ 13 is ≤2016; also 17). Then n=p contributes exactly one factor p and every factor kp+1 is coprime to p, so v_p(P(p)) = 1. Hence each prime appears exactly once in the gcd. Answer: 2·3·5·7·11·13·17 = 510510.
